title: Sequence length sweep - 32 frames
research_question: Does reducing sequence length from 64 to 32 frames affect WLASL30 recognition accuracy under the same GRU+Attention architecture?

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU

main_findings: Top-1 61.76% is the highest of the three seed=42 runs (64f: 55.88%, 96f: 58.82%), but the margin is within the documented K-Fold Top-1 standard deviation of +/-4.5%, so this single-seed result cannot be read as evidence that shorter sequences help.
Top-5 88.24% is comparable to the 96f run (85.29%) and clearly above the 64f run (73.53%), again pointing to seed-level variance on the 34-sample test set rather than a length effect.
Training ran for 88 epochs with early stopping triggering at epoch 58, the longest of the three lengths; 32-frame inputs did not converge faster despite carrying less temporal information.
Val Top-1 is 66.07%, identical to the 64f seed=42 run, suggesting the Top-1 gap is localised to the test split.
limitations: Single seed (42); no statistical significance can be claimed against the 64f or 96f runs.
Test set has only 34 samples, so each misclassification shifts Top-1 by ~2.94 percentage points.
Early stopping with patience=30 may interact differently with shorter sequences, but this cannot be diagnosed from a single run.
next_actions: Re-run with seeds 123 and 2026 and report mean +/- std before drawing any conclusion about 32 vs 64 frames.
After multi-seed aggregation, inspect the per-class confusion matrix to check whether short sequences preferentially hurt signs with long duration.
